q: The ability to move in animals is made possible by the combination of a semi rigid skeletal system with joints that act as ____ .
e: The ability to move in animals is made possible by the combination of a semi rigid skeletal system with joints that act as hinges. Hinges is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Muscular action produces a change in body shape, which places a force on different parts of the ____ environment.
e: Muscular action produces a change in body shape, which places a force on different parts of the outside environment. Outside is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For example, when a horse runs, its feet contact the ground, and the force they exert moves its body ____ .
e: For example, when a horse runs, its feet contact the ground, and the force they exert moves its body forward. Forward is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In a similar way, when a bird takes off into flight, its wings exert force on the ____ .
e: In a similar way, when a bird takes off into flight, its wings exert force on the air. Air is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Locomotion in earthworms involves a fluid-filled central body cavity or coelom encompassed by two sets of muscles in the body wall: circular muscles and ____ muscles.
e: Locomotion in earthworms involves a fluid-filled central body cavity or coelom encompassed by two sets of muscles in the body wall: circular muscles and longitudinal muscles. Longitudinal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Short and bristle-like structures called ____ are on the underside of a worm’s body.
e: Short and bristle-like structures called setae are on the underside of a worm’s body. Setae is the idea that completes this fact.

q: This locomotion process proceeds as waves of circular-muscle contraction followed by waves of longitudinal muscle contraction which pass ____ .
e: This locomotion process proceeds as waves of circular-muscle contraction followed by waves of longitudinal muscle contraction which pass backward. Backward is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the anterior end, circular muscles contract and longitudinal muscles relax, causing setae to lose contact with the ____ .
e: In the anterior end, circular muscles contract and longitudinal muscles relax, causing setae to lose contact with the ground. Ground is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Next, the circular muscles contract; the longitudinal muscles relax, causing the anterior of the body to swell and setae to anchor the ____ .
e: Next, the circular muscles contract; the longitudinal muscles relax, causing the anterior of the body to swell and setae to anchor the ground. Ground is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The body region behind the anterior end is pulled forward, and setae prevent slipping ____ of the front end.
e: The body region behind the anterior end is pulled forward, and setae prevent slipping backward of the front end. Backward is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Jumping in grasshoppers involves the flexor and ____ muscles attached to the internal surface of the exoskeleton.
e: Jumping in grasshoppers involves the flexor and extensor muscles attached to the internal surface of the exoskeleton. Extensor is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When the flexor muscle contracts, the leg jerks backwards, propelling the grasshopper ____ .
e: When the flexor muscle contracts, the leg jerks backwards, propelling the grasshopper forward. Forward is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of raising and lowering wings in flight is achieved by the alternate contraction of extensor muscles and ____ muscles.
e: The movement of raising and lowering wings in flight is achieved by the alternate contraction of extensor muscles and flexor muscles. Flexor is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fish have a streamlined body shape for swimming in water to reduce ____ .
e: Fish have a streamlined body shape for swimming in water to reduce friction. Friction is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fish move forward as a result of the contraction and relaxation of muscles called ____ on either side of the body.
e: Fish move forward as a result of the contraction and relaxation of muscles called myotomes on either side of the body. Myotomes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pectoral fins are used to steer the fish, while pelvic fins are used to balance the fish and prevent it from ____ .
e: Pectoral fins are used to steer the fish, while pelvic fins are used to balance the fish and prevent it from diving. Diving is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The frog’s powerful hind legs are adapted for both swimming and ____ .
e: The frog’s powerful hind legs are adapted for both swimming and leaping. Leaping is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The strong extensor muscles of the thigh contract, extending the limb and thrusting the foot against the ground or against the ____ .
e: The strong extensor muscles of the thigh contract, extending the limb and thrusting the foot against the ground or against the water. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most birds have approximately ____ different muscles, mainly controlling the wings, skin, and legs.
e: Most birds have approximately 175 different muscles, mainly controlling the wings, skin, and legs. 175 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: During flight, a bird moves its wings in a pattern of upstrokes and ____ .
e: During flight, a bird moves its wings in a pattern of upstrokes and downstrokes. Downstrokes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The antagonistic muscle pair of pectoral and supracoracoideus forms the major flight muscles, allowing for effective wing ____ .
e: The antagonistic muscle pair of pectoral and supracoracoideus forms the major flight muscles, allowing for effective wing movement. Movement is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In humans, there are about ____ skeletal muscles that function in antagonistic pairs for locomotion and movement.
e: In humans, there are about 650 skeletal muscles that function in antagonistic pairs for locomotion and movement. 650 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One prominent example pair of muscles is biceps brachii and triceps brachii in the upper arm, where contraction of biceps brachii ____ the forearm towards the upper arm.
e: One prominent example pair of muscles is biceps brachii and triceps brachii in the upper arm, where contraction of biceps brachii flexes the forearm towards the upper arm. Flexes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When the triceps brachii is relaxed, flexion happens at the hinge joint at the ____ .
e: When the triceps brachii is relaxed, flexion happens at the hinge joint at the elbow. Elbow is the idea that completes this fact.

q: But when the biceps relaxes and the triceps contracts, the forearm is pulled away from the ____ .
e: But when the biceps relaxes and the triceps contracts, the forearm is pulled away from the upper arm. Upper arm is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Another example pair of muscles is the hamstring and quadriceps muscles in the thigh of the legs, where contraction of the hamstring and relaxing of the quadriceps flex the leg at the ____ .
e: Another example pair of muscles is the hamstring and quadriceps muscles in the thigh of the legs, where contraction of the hamstring and relaxing of the quadriceps flex the leg at the knee. Knee is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Next, the leg is extended at the knee by contraction of the quadriceps and relaxing of the hamstring muscles, showing the action of ____ pairs.
e: Next, the leg is extended at the knee by contraction of the quadriceps and relaxing of the hamstring muscles, showing the action of antagonistic pairs. Antagonistic is the idea that completes this fact.
